title: What you're actually trying to do
hints: There's no on-screen checklist, but the game does have a concrete win condition, and it's tied to a number you can already see at the top of the screen.
Exploring for its own sake won't finish the game — you need to find the dungeon's treasures and get each one to a very specific piece of furniture back at the house.

The objective is to explore the Great Underground Empire, recover all its treasures, and bring each one home to the living room's trophy case — simply carrying a treasure isn't enough, it has to be cased. Do that thoroughly enough and the game itself reveals the final step needed to win (see 'Getting the most out of your treasures' and 'Reaching the endgame' for the specifics).

title: Items you shouldn't leave without
hints: Several ordinary-looking objects turn out to be required, not optional, once you're underground — most are easy to miss if you're only hunting for treasures.
A weapon, a light source, something with a strong smell, and a few small tools for very specific machines are all worth grabbing early, even before you know exactly why.

Keep the sword and lamp (from the trophy case) on you at all times underground. Also collect: the garlic (kitchen shelf, keeps the bat away), the knife and rope (attic), the bell, candles and matches (for the Hades ritual — candles double as emergency light), the wrench (Maintenance Room, for the dam), and the screwdriver (for the coal mine's machine). The lamp's battery is finite (it starts dimming after roughly 100 turns of use), so turn it off whenever you're somewhere already lit, and pick up the ivory torch later as a renewable backup light source.

title: Managing what you carry
hints: You can't just grab everything you find — there's a real weight limit on what you can hold at once, so hauling treasures works better as several smaller trips than one giant haul.

Getting wounded in a fight temporarily makes you weaker AND lowers how much you can carry until you heal back up over the next several turns — an overloaded pack can suddenly become 'too heavy' right after a fight for reasons that have nothing to do with what you picked up. Also, the very first time you go down through the trap door, it always slams shut and locks behind you no matter what — the only way back up immediately afterward is climbing the chimney, and that only works carrying nothing but the lit lamp.

Treat it as round trips, not one expedition: grab a manageable load, bring it straight to the trophy case (see 'Getting the most out of your treasures'), then head back down for more — nothing is lost by doing this, and it's basically required once you've found more than a few treasures. If you're overloaded, dropping the excess in a room you already know is safe works as a temporary stash. Because that first trip down the trap door is a one-way slam, don't carry anything down with you on that first descent that you'd hate to leave behind if the chimney (lamp-only) turns out to be your fastest way back. Keep a weapon on you at all times once you're underground regardless — the troll fight is mandatory and can't be talked or sneaked past, and the thief can turn up and attack whether or not you're looking for a fight (the cyclops is the one exception: he can't be fought at all, only scared off with a word).

title: How fighting works
hints: Combat isn't a coin flip — your own condition and the weapon in your hand both matter more than you might expect.

Getting hurt only weakens you temporarily (you recover over the next several turns), and your overall fighting ability actually depends on how much you've accomplished in the game so far. Retreating from a losing fight is always an option.

Your effective combat strength rises with your score, so treasure-hunting before a big fight genuinely helps. Wounds heal automatically after a few turns — type 'diagnose' anytime to check your condition and how close to death you are. The sword is the troll's classic match and the knife is the thief's; the cyclops can't be fought with a weapon at all. If you're losing to the thief, handing him a treasure momentarily distracts him, giving you a bit of breathing room.

title: Getting started above ground
hints: Look closely at everything near the house before you go inside — small objects here matter later, and one of them explains the local geography.
The front door won't budge, but the house has more than one way in. Walk all the way around it and examine what you find on each side.
Go around to the kitchen window at the rear of the house, open it, and enter that way.

title: Not getting lost in the forest
hints: The forest around the house isn't actually a maze -- it's small and its layout never changes -- but several different rooms print the exact same "Forest" description, and two entirely separate rooms are both just called "Clearing," so it's very easy to feel turned around even though you aren't.

The forest is really a loop wrapped around the house: the west, north, and south sides of the house each open directly into it, and the east side opens onto a clearing that continues toward a canyon. All of these connect to each other, so heading back toward any side of the house you recognize will get you out. The one real dead end is pushing further into impassable mountains -- once you're facing those, every direction just leads back to the same spot, so don't keep pushing past them looking for a way through.

Concretely: West of House leads into the forest, and from there you can reach a path (with a climbable tree worth investigating) to the north, or work your way south and around to the south side of the house. East of House leads to a different clearing than the one you may find deeper in the forest -- don't confuse the two if a hint mentions burning something at 'the clearing.' If you're ever unsure where you are, walking toward the house is always safe, since every forest room is only one or two moves from a side of it.

title: Finding the way underground
hints: Something in the living room is covering more than just the floor. Furniture and rugs are always worth a closer look.
Move the rug in the living room aside instead of just looking at it.
Move the rug to reveal a trap door, then open the trap door and go down. Bring a light source — the case with the lamp and sword should already be open.

title: Light before you go underground
hints: The Great Underground Empire has no windows. Anything you take with you should include a way to see.
There's a brass lantern in the living room, inside furniture you can open.
Open the trophy case in the living room, take the lantern and the sword, and turn the lantern on before descending through the trap door.

title: The knife and rope upstairs
hints: The house has one more floor you probably haven't explored, reachable from the room with the stove — though it's pitch dark up there.
Bring your lit lamp and go up from the Kitchen. Two items worth taking are waiting: one on a table, one coiled in a corner.

Go up from the Kitchen (lamp lit — the Attic is dark) and take the nasty knife from the table and the large coil of rope from the corner, then head back down. The rope is what lets you descend safely from the Dome Room later on.

title: The troll blocking the passage
hints: The troll won't let you pass peacefully, and bare hands aren't going to help.
Make sure you're carrying the sword from the trophy case before you meet him, and draw it if the game doesn't do so automatically in combat.
Fight the troll with the sword (try 'kill troll with sword' or just 'attack troll' repeatedly) until he's defeated; retreating and returning to heal is fine if you're losing.

title: Getting past the Cyclops
hints: Brute force doesn't work on him, and he doesn't respond to ordinary conversation either.
He reacts strongly to a very particular word — something from a much older story about someone who blinded a cyclops.
Say 'ulysses' (or 'odysseus') to the cyclops. He'll flee in terror and even knock a hole in a wall that shortcuts you toward the living room.

title: The room with the strange echo
hints: Ordinary commands seem to just bounce back at you strangely in one particular room. Try something other than movement or object commands.
The room itself is the puzzle, not an object in it. Consider what you'd naturally shout in a room like this.
Say 'echo' while in the Loud Room. This quiets the water noise from the nearby dam long enough for you to also read the marble engraving that helps at the endgame.

title: The dam and the reservoir
hints: There's machinery on the dam that clearly used to control the water level, but it's stuck.
Look for a small tool left behind near the control panel — you'll need it in hand, not just nearby.

Take the wrench in the Maintenance Room, go to the Dam, and turn the bolt with the wrench to raise or lower the reservoir's water level as needed. Push the yellow button in Maintenance first to light the room, and be careful about being in the reservoir when you drain or fill it.

title: The bat in the coal mine area
hints: One of the underground rooms has a creature that will interfere with you if you're not carrying the right thing.
Something pungent from the kitchen keeps unwanted flying creatures away.
Carry the garlic (from the kitchen, up on a shelf) through the bat's room and it will leave you alone.

title: Turning coal into a diamond
hints: The coal mine's machine looks built to transform whatever you feed it, but it won't run without the right tool in hand.
You'll need to be holding a screwdriver to work the switch, and you'll need something to put inside first.

In the Machine Room: open the lid, put the piece of coal inside, close the lid, then turn the switch with the screwdriver. Drop the screwdriver, open the lid again, and take the diamond that's replaced the coal.

title: Dealing with the thief
hints: A shifty character wanders the dungeon, stealing your treasures and attacking you. Fighting him early, unprepared, usually goes badly.
He's most dangerous face-to-face before you're strong enough; many players avoid him until they have a good weapon and are willing to lose a fight or two to gain experience.

Engage the thief with the sword once you're reasonably confident (repeated fights make your character tougher). When you finally defeat him in his treasure room, he drops everything he's stolen, including anything sealed inside the egg.

title: The jewel-encrusted egg
hints: The egg you find in a tree is fragile, and forcing it open yourself ruins the valuable thing inside.
You don't have the delicate touch needed to open it safely — but you know someone who does, even though he's not exactly a friend.
Give the egg, unopened, to the thief. He'll open it properly. Defeat him later to recover the egg and the golden canary inside intact.

title: Getting the most out of your treasures
hints: Simply finding a treasure only earns part of its value — the rest is waiting for you back at the house.
Treasures score extra points the moment they're actually placed inside a specific piece of furniture in the Living Room, not just carried around in your pack.

Bring every treasure home and put it in the trophy case — each one scores bonus points beyond its 'found' value on top of what you got for finding it. Zork I has 19 treasures worth a maximum of 350 points combined, and you need essentially all of them cased to unlock the ending.

title: Entering the Land of the Dead
hints: The entrance near the cyclops area is guarded by something that isn't physical — ordinary weapons won't help.
You'll need a specific ritual, and the tools for it are all found elsewhere in the dungeon: something to ring, something to read from, and something to light.

At the Entrance to Hades, ring the bell (it becomes red hot, so drop it immediately), light the candles, then read the black book. This exorcises the spirits and opens the way to the Land of the Dead.

title: Getting down from the Dome Room
hints: One large, round room overlooks a long drop to a room below, with no visible stairs down.
You'll need something long to lower yourself with, tied off to something sturdy that's already there.
In the Dome Room, tie the rope (from the attic) to the railing, then climb down the rope to reach the Torch Room below.

title: The Egyptian Room's coffin
hints: Deep in a temple complex is a room decorated like a tomb, holding something valuable and something far too heavy to haul around.
The gold coffin itself won't fit down every passage nearby, but what's sitting inside it isn't attached.

In the Egyptian Room, take the coffin, open it, and take the sceptre from inside. Leave the coffin behind before heading further down through the Temple's Altar — the passage there refuses to let you carry the coffin through. (Praying at the Altar is also a free, instant trip back to the forest if you ever need an escape.)

title: The mirror rooms
hints: Two identical rooms, far apart in the dungeon, both happen to have an enormous mirror covering a wall — that's unlikely to be a coincidence.
Try interacting with the mirror itself, not just looking into it.

Rub the mirror in either Mirror Room to instantly teleport to the other one — a fast shortcut between the reservoir/river area and the temple/coal-mine area. Don't damage the mirror, or you'll strand yourself and lose the shortcut for good.

title: Crossing the Frigid River safely
hints: A wide, swift river blocks part of the dungeon, and swimming, wading, or leaping across it all end badly.
You'll need something that floats, inflated with the right tool — and you must empty your hands of anything sharp before you climb aboard.

Inflate the plastic boat with the air pump (both near the Dam Base), drop any weapons or sharp objects first (boarding with one punctures the boat), get in, and say 'launch'. The current carries you downstream on its own — just watch for a red buoy floating by and grab it before you land.

title: The buoy floating in the river
hints: Something small and red drifts past while you're out on the water — probably worth grabbing before it's out of reach.
It's not just a marker; it's built to hold something inside.
Take the red buoy while riding the river in the boat, then open it once you're safely ashore to find an emerald inside.

title: Crossing the rainbow for the pot of gold
hints: The rainbow over Aragain Falls looks purely decorative — until you're holding the right treasure.
Something you found inside a coffin does more than just look nice when you wave it in the right spot.

At Aragain Falls (or the End of Rainbow), wave the sceptre to make the rainbow solid enough to walk on. Cross it to reach the End of Rainbow and take the pot of gold. Don't wave the sceptre again while standing on the rainbow itself — that dissolves it right out from under you.

title: Navigating the twisty maze
hints: All the rooms here look identical, and normal exploration will just get you lost or looped back to where you started.

Dropping something distinctive in each room to map it by trial and error works, but you don't have to -- this particular maze has one specific, fixed way through it from the Troll Room, regardless of how turned around the identical descriptions make you feel.

From the Troll Room, go west, south, east, then up -- that fixed four-move path always leads to the room with the skeleton, no mapping required. There you'll find a leather bag of coins (a treasure), a rusty knife, and a skeleton key; the burned-out lantern lying there is junk, skip it. From that room, go southwest, up, east, up, then northeast to reach a grating; unlock it with the skeleton key, open it, and go up to pop out in a clearing above ground -- a shortcut that lets you skip the maze entirely on future trips in or out.

title: Reaching the endgame
hints: Finishing the game isn't triggered by reaching a place — it's triggered by something you've been building the whole time. Leaving even one treasure uncased will stop you short.
Once your trophy case truly holds (almost) everything of value and your score has topped out, the game lets you know something's changed. Pay attention next time you're back above ground.

Deposit every treasure in the trophy case until your score reaches the maximum (350). A voice whispers that the final secret lies with your treasures, and a new path opens southwest from West of House. Follow it to the Stone Barrow and go in (or west) to win the game.
